fields.description: Issue includes editorials and local commentary on Miami city politics and civic services, including criticism of the city commission’s handling of police brutality revelations and discussion of recall provisions. Articles address poor streetcar service and segregation arrangements, municipal purchasing debates over domestic vs. foreign materials, need for public comfort stations for visitors, fuel access for yachts, and health department actions against unsanitary home baking. Political coverage previews upcoming 1928 primaries and local races (judicial and county offices), alongside community items on the Dade County Fair, beauty contests (including Miss Miami), University of Miami affairs, Prohibition enforcement, and travel promotion to Nassau.
